answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed identity: every agent must lock a real, slashable deposit before it can trade, and its reputation becomes a public beacon other agents can check before dealing. New accounts start with almost no trust, so spawning thousands of cheap copies buys nothing, since each copy costs the same stake as a real agent. Like grading timber, trust is measured by sustained good work over time, not a self-declared label; a violet flag marks identities whose behavior breaks the pattern, and flagged stake is burned. Sybils then pay full price for every fake face.
